sara_dev: Hey folks — saw a pattern in prod where tenants with lots of long-context requests get effectively starved during KV-heavy windows. short requests fly, long ones queue and then get ejected by our load-shed. :frowning_face:

mike_infra: Can you paste a small perf trace? is this KV eviction or batch admission bias? :thinking:

sara_dev: Minimal trace:
```
[2026-03-10T14:03:12Z] tenant=acme req=R123 len=10240 queued=230ms admitted=3ms batch_size=12 kernel=quant-opt kv_hit=false
[2026-03-10T14:03:12Z] tenant=mini req=R456 len=256 queued=8ms admitted=2ms batch_size=12 kernel=fastpath kv_hit=true
[... repeated pattern ...]
```
seems like admissions prefer short sequences (fastpath + kv hits) and long sequences get pushed later, then hit token-budget load-shed.

priyanka_ml: This matches the microbench we ran — when KV miss rate increases, our continuous-batcher forms bigger homogeneous short-preferring batches because kernel-selection greedily groups by short-path throughput. Long sequences get lower token credits and eventually time out.

dan_runtime: Proposal: token-lottery admission. Instead of deterministic credits per tenant per epoch, run a small randomized lottery where each queued request draws tickets proportional to an adjustable weight (sequence length inverse + tenant priority). Winners get admits first. Should reduce pathological lockout.

olivia_sre: Love the idea. Any downside? randomness might increase latency variance which our SLOs hate. We need bounded variance.

priyanka_ml: We can cap per-tenant variance by combining lottery with min-guarantees. Two knobs: guaranteed tokens per window (absolute) + lottery pool for leftover credits. That keeps tail bounded.

mike_infra: Also need kernel-awareness — when lottery picks a long seq, runtime must choose a kernel path that doesn't blow up latency. Maybe prefer hybrid-kernel (prefetch KV + async attention) for lottery-confirmed long requests.

kv-bot: INFO: current_batcher_config: {"window_ms":12,"max_batch":64,"min_admit":1,"credit_refill":900} — toggles available: lottery_enabled=false

sara_dev: Sketch of a toggle/experiment command: `./deploy-cfg set batcher.lottery_enabled=true batcher.lottery_pool=0.15 batcher.min_guarantee=0.02` — start with small pool (15% of refilled credits) and min guarantee 2% per tenant.

dan_runtime: For telemetry, record: pre_admit_queue_depth, post_admit_queue_depth, admit_via_lottery(boolean), kernel_chosen, kv_hit_rate, tenant_token_balance. We'll need a new trace tag to correlate with rollouts.

priyanka_ml: Ran a short sim overnight with 10k mixed requests: tail p99 latency for long-requests dropped from 3.2s to 1.1s, median unchanged, variance up ~12%. KV hit-rate improved slightly due to fewer evictions.

olivia_sre: Can we gate this behind canary plus automated abort if p99_long > baseline * 1.3? I want playbooks for rollback.

mike_infra: Yeah — add an automated guard in console: if any safety metric regresses beyond threshold, auto-revert flag. Also add a per-tenant opt-out label for enterprise customers.

sara_dev: Next steps I volunteer for: (1) implement lottery admission in batcher (2) runtime kernel hint path for lottery-wins (3) add telemetry tags and canary rule. Will open a PR and a small design doc.

dan_runtime: Ping me on the PR for kernel hint integration — I'll wire kernel chooser to accept `prefer_hybrid=true` for those admits.

priyanka_ml: I'll run longer sims across varying KV miss profiles and attach heatmaps.

olivia_sre: I'll draft the rollback playbook + SLO gating rule. :thumbsup:

kv-bot: WARNING: scheduled maintenance 2026-03-12 02:00Z may affect canary nodes.

sara_dev: Noted. Will try to avoid starting the canary until after maintenance. Thanks all. :eyes:
